html:
Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in the West African savanna, with its capital at Ouagadougou. It was called Upper Volta until 1984.

Its largest people, the Mossi, built the Mossi kingdoms from about the 15th century; they long resisted the Muslim empires to the north. France conquered them in 1896. It made Upper Volta a colony within French West Africa in 1919, split it among neighbours in 1932, and rebuilt it in 1947.

  • 1960: independence as the Republic of Upper Volta.
  • 1966 onward: a run of coups.
  • 1983 to 1987: Thomas Sankara led a revolutionary government and renamed the country Burkina Faso, "land of upright people".
  • 1987: Sankara was killed in a coup; Blaise Compaoré ruled until a popular uprising in 2014.
  • Since 2015: jihadist insurgency; two coups in 2022.

Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, Africa's largest film festival.
sum: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in the West African savanna, with its capital at Ouagadougou. It was called Upper Volta until 1984.
